He initially entered a plea of not guilty. However, he later appeared in court, changing his plea to no contest and the judge adjudicated him guilty on all charges. He was sentenced to 13 days in jail, with credit for 11 days already served, followed by 12 months of probation. His driver's license was revoked for six months, and his vehicle was ordered to be impounded for 10 days. Additionally, he was required to complete DUI school in a high-risk driver's course and pay various fines, court costs, and attorney fees. Following the incident, she was charged with battery on a law enforcement officer in disorderly intoxication. She was held on a $3,000 bond, which she later posted. Though she initially entered a plea of not guilty, she ultimately changed her plea to guilty on both charges. She was sentenced to two days in jail, 30 days in a day work program, and 36 months of probation. Additionally, she was ordered to attend an 18-week anger management program, submit a DNA sample to the state law enforcement database, and pay $733 in restitution, alongside court costs and attorney fees.
